title: Grade 4 French — Tue, May 19
description: Les articles — Day 2 of 5: Indefinite articles (un, une, des)
subject: french

questions.question: Which indefinite article is used with masculine singular nouns?
questions.explanation: 'Un' = a/an (masculine singular). Un livre (a book), un chien (a dog).

questions.question: Which indefinite article is used with feminine singular nouns?
questions.explanation: 'Une' = a/an (feminine singular). Une table (a table), une fleur (a flower).

questions.question: Which indefinite article is used for ALL plural nouns?
questions.explanation: 'Des' = some/any (plural, both genders). Des livres (some books), des tables (some tables).

questions.question: Fill in: 'J'ai ___ chien.' (a dog — masculine)
questions.explanation: 'J'ai un chien.' = I have a dog. Chien is masculine → un.

questions.question: Fill in: 'Voici ___ maison.' (a house — feminine)
questions.explanation: 'Voici une maison.' = Here is a house. Maison is feminine → une.

questions.question: Fill in: 'Il a ___ amis.' (some friends — plural)
questions.explanation: 'Il a des amis.' = He has some friends. Amis is plural → des.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'le/la' and 'un/une'?
options: No difference — they are the same
Le/la is for plural; un/une for singular
questions.explanation: Le chat = THE (specific) cat. Un chat = A cat (any cat). Definite (le/la) vs Indefinite (un/une).

questions.question: Translate: 'I see a bird.'
questions.explanation: 'Je vois un oiseau.' = I see a bird (any bird, not specific). Oiseau is masculine → un.

questions.question: Translate: 'She eats an apple.'
questions.explanation: 'Elle mange une pomme.' = She eats an apple. Pomme is feminine → une.

questions.question: Translate: 'I have some books.'
questions.explanation: 'J'ai des livres.' = I have some books. Livres is plural → des.

questions.question: Which is correct: 'Je veux un/une café'?
questions.explanation: 'Je veux un café.' = I want a coffee. Café is masculine → un.

questions.question: Change to plural: 'J'ai un livre et une table.' →
options: J'ai un livres et une tables.
J'ai des livres et des tables.
J'ai les livres et les tables.
J'ai des livre et des table.
questions.explanation: 'J'ai des livres et des tables.' Un→des, une→des, nouns add -s in plural.

questions.question: Choose the correct article for 'étudiante' (female student, feminine):
questions.explanation: 'Une étudiante' = a female student. Étudiante is feminine singular → une.

questions.question: Translate: 'There is a cat in the garden.'
options: Il y a le chat dans le jardin.
Il y a un chat dans le jardin.
Il y a une chat dans le jardin.
Il y a des chat dans le jardin.
questions.explanation: 'Il y a un chat dans le jardin.' = There is a cat (indefinite = any cat) in the garden.

questions.question: Fill in both: 'Voici ___ fille et ___ garçon.' (a girl, a boy)
questions.explanation: 'Voici une fille et un garçon.' Une (feminine) for fille, un (masculine) for garçon.
